newsitem.title: CANADA: Laidlaw to acquire American Medical for US$1.12 bln.
newsitem.headline: Laidlaw to acquire American Medical for US$1.12 bln.

text.p: Canadian waste and transportation giant Laidlaw Inc. said on Monday that it plans to acquire Colorado-based American Medical Response Inc. in a US$1.12 billion cash deal and merge it with its California-based MedTrans ambulance services unit.

Laidlaw, based in Burlington, Ontario, also said it has signed a letter of intent to sell its South Carolina-based Environmental Services unit for cash, shares and debt to Rollins Environmental Services Inc. of Delaware.
Laidlaw said it would a tender offer within the next five business days and the deal is expected to close in February.
AMR and MedTrans -- North America's top two health-care transportation firms -- have a combined $1.3 billion in annual revenues and a 14 percent market share of the $10 billion industry.
The new company will continue to operate under the name American Medical Response Inc and remain headquartered in Aurora, Colorado, a suburb of Denver.
Laidlaw chief executive officer James Bullock said AMR would extend Laidlaw's reach into 11 new U.S. states and broaden the range of transportation services it offered.

"It more than doubles Laidlaw's participation in a growing industry which we will expand beyond traditional transportation services into a variety of related emergency and non-emergency healthcare services," Bullock said.
He said AMR would immediately add to Laidlaw's earnings, but he declined to give a specific forecast.

In the other transaction, Laidlaw said it has signed a letter of intent to sell its South Carolina-based Environmental Services unit for cash, stock and debt to Rollins Environmental Services of Wilmington, Delaware.
Laidlaw will receive $400 million in cash, 120 million Rollins' common shares, and a $350 million, 12-year, five percent convertible debenture.

Upon completion, the operations of both firms will be combined into a new company -- Laidlaw Environmental Services Inc. -- which will be 66-percent-owned by Laidlaw and continue to trade on the New York Stock Exchange.
Both boards have approved the transaction to create a bigger environmental services provider with over $900 million in projected annual revenues.
Bullock said the deal "offers Laidlaw and Rollins shareholders the opportunity to participate in the growth of a well-capitalized, stronger, independent, publicly-traded entity..."
Rollins shareholders will vote on the transaction at a special meeting expected to be held in March.
